blocks.heading: Operations Manager Actually Does All Day
rows: Process design and ownership

Building, documenting, and improving the standard operating procedure for a recurring business function, order fulfilment, onboarding, service delivery, or production flow. An operations manager is judged on whether a process still works when they are not in the room, not on how many fires they personally put out.
Vendor, logistics, and resource coordination

Negotiating and managing vendor contracts, tracking delivery timelines, allocating budget and headcount across competing priorities, and stepping in the moment a supplier, courier, or resource plan breaks down mid-cycle.
Cross-functional coordination

Sitting between sales, finance, product, HR, and the frontline team, translating what each function needs into a plan the others can actually execute against. This is the part job postings undersell, most escalations land on the ops manager because they are the one person who can see the whole system.
KPI ownership

Owning a real number, turnaround time, cost per unit, fulfilment accuracy, customer resolution time, utilisation rate, and being accountable for moving it, not just reporting it. This is the single biggest difference between an operations executive and an operations manager: the executive tracks the number, the manager owns the outcome behind it.

blocks.heading: Entry Routes Into Operations Management in India
rows: Typical starting title
Operations executive, operations analyst, or process associate
Supply chain analyst, business analyst, or a fresh BBA/MBA graduate hired directly into a management-track ops role
Time to reach "operations manager" title
Roughly 3-5 years, sometimes faster in fast-growing e-commerce or startup operations teams that promote on outcome, not tenure
Can be immediate for MBA graduates hired through campus placement into an operations or general management track, but the first 1-2 years still function like a steep on-the-job apprenticeship
What actually gets you promoted
A track record of owning a real KPI and moving it, documented process improvements, and visibly handling escalations without a manager stepping in

Structured problem-solving ability proven through case studies or internships, plus the same on-the-ground KPI ownership once inside the company, the degree opens the door, it does not replace the proof
Risk if you skip it
Staying an "executive" for too long because nobody has handed you real ownership, you have to ask for it, not wait for it
Landing a management-sounding title with no real operating experience underneath it, which shows up hard the first time a process actually breaks

items.text: How to become an operations manager in India comes down to two real entry routes: climb from an operations executive or analyst role by deliberately owning a KPI and documenting process improvements, or enter laterally through a supply chain specialisation, BBA, or MBA that gets you into a management track faster.

Proving you can own a live process, coordinate people who do not report to you, and move a real number is what actually gets you hired and promoted, and it is also what turns this role into a genuinely high-income skill instead of a coordinator's job with a bigger-sounding title.
The job is process design, vendor and logistics coordination, cross-functional problem-solving, and owning a real KPI, not general task management.
